item.title: [SwiftHFR] Favoris first scroll: guard the list body against scroll-driven runs (#1015)
item.body:
Refs #1015 (what is left: the operator's live check on the iPhone of a build that includes #1017 / f53cb5df, the measured "no hitch over one frame"; the issue closes after it)
Claim: mac/M1
Author model: Claude Opus 5.5 (mac/M1-i1015-opus)
Reviewer model: fable-5.2 (mac/M1-r1046-fable: REQUEST CHANGES on b7cd3901; APPROVE on 1fc0500b, the head)

### Problem
In Favoris the first scroll stutters, while the large title leaves and the tab bar minimises. It stutters again on the way back up. The stutter grows with the number of sections and rows.

### Cause (measured in a hosted probe, simulator, no logged-in session)
I counted body evaluations and layout passes in a hosted Favoris tab: `TabView` with `.tabBarMinimizeBehavior(.onScrollDown)`, `NavigationSplitView`, `TopicsColumn`, and 10 categories × 8 topics. The scroll was driven 5 pt per frame. I also stepped the top and bottom safe area to stand in for the bars moving.

| Build | List body runs | Row closures | Header builds | Row layout passes (size/place) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before #1017 (the body reads the title visibility, as `@State titleIsVisible` did) | 1 per crossing | 25 | 10 (every section) | 24 / 36 |
| `dev-swift` today (after #1017) | 0 | 6 (only new rows entering) | 0 | 6 / 9 |

- Before #1017, each crossing of the large title re-ran `TopicListView.body`. That run recomputed `displayedGroups`, rebuilt every section header and re-applied every realised row's swipe, menu and accessibility modifiers. It also laid the rows out again. The cost is O(sections + visible rows), it hits at both crossings, and it lands on the same frames as the tab-bar transition, which fits the operator's report.
- Since #1017 (merged 2026-11-17 11:38 UTC, "Refs #1015"), `TitleVisibility` is read only by `PillSlot`. A crossing redraws the pill and nothing else.
- On today's head, scrolling and the safe-area steps (bottom and top) trigger no body run and no row layout in the list, header, menu or pager. The pager modifier, the header margins and the Favoris options menu were all checked.
- So the cause the code shows is already fixed on `dev-swift`. The operator's report may predate #1017 (LESSONS 46). Check that the device build includes `f53cb5df`.

Not reproducible here: a programmatic scroll does not trigger the real tab-bar minimise. Whether the real minimise moves the content's safe area on a device is not measured. If the stutter remains on a build that includes #1017, the next step is an Instruments trace on the device.

### What changed, and why this wide and no wider
- `TopicListView` with its new `TopicListView+RenderSeam.swift` (kept in its own file to stay under the 400-line `file_length` limit): a test seam. `counting(_:_:)` passes its value through and, in debug builds, counts one build of the list body, of a section header (by group id) or of a row (by topic id), per model. It also keeps the list's `TitleVisibility` so the test can check that the crossings really happen.
  - The calls sit in existing expressions (`let loader = …`, `let isSuper = …`, and the header's returned view), so no `let _ =` is needed in a view builder, which `redundant_discardable_let` forbids. `.swiftlint.yml` is unchanged.
  - Keys are never removed, and an identifier can be reused once its model is freed. The test therefore reads deltas from a baseline.
  - Release builds keep only the pass-through.
- `TitleVisibility.report(_:)`: the large title's `onScrollVisibilityChange` goes through it, and debug builds count the reports.
- `FavorisScrollHostedTests`: the regression guard.
- No behaviour change. No change to the large title, the pill or the tab-bar minimise.
- The other suspects in the code study were left alone because the probe found no cost from them: rows not `Equatable`, no `.listStyle`, `DensityHeaderMargin`, `PagerBarModifier`.

### Tests
`FavorisScrollHostedTests/scrollLeavesTheListAlone()` hosts the app's `FavoritesTabView` (with a fake `ReaderServices`) under a `TabView` that minimises on scroll. Left out: the other tabs and the root's environment.
- **Down leg:** 300 pt past the large title, frame by frame. The title must report it left. Expected: no list body run, no section header build, and no rebuild of any row that was on screen at landing.
- **Safe-area stand-in:** the top and bottom safe area are stepped. Expected: no build at all.
- **Up leg:** back up until the title reports it is back (at least 2 reports). Expected: no list body run and no header build. Rows coming back on screen are built legitimately.
- **Positive controls:** the seam counted the body, the headers and the rows on screen at landing, and the title's reports (at least 1 down, at least 2 round trip).
- **Covered:** the large-title crossings in both directions, and the safe-area stand-in. **Not covered:** the real Liquid Glass tab-bar minimise. A programmatic scroll does not trigger it, and the stand-in is not shown to be what it does. That part is the device check.
- **Mutation runs** (a per-frame read of `titleVisibility.isHeaderVisible`). Each one fails:
  - In the list body: the body runs once going down and twice over the round trip. Every header is rebuilt, and the rows on screen are rebuilt.
  - In `header(_:title:)`: every header is rebuilt at each crossing, and the rows are rebuilt too.
  - In a row (`rows(_:)`): every row on screen is rebuilt at the crossing.
- The suite passed 3 times out of 3 on the head `1fc0500b`. The mutations and the whole `SwiftHFRTests` target ran on `bb0620ee` (1896 tests in 241 suites passed, iPhone 18 Pro simulator, iOS 27.0); `1fc0500b` only turns a test helper's triple into a struct for SwiftLint.
- SwiftLint is green on `1fc0500b`. Round 1 took three commits: the review fixes, then two SwiftLint follow-ups (`file_length`, `function_body_length`, `large_tuple`) that only CI's linter reports.

### Device check (operator, iPhone, 120 Hz, on a build that includes #1017)
- First scroll of Favoris, down and back to the top, with many categories expanded, compared with Catégories.
- The large title still collapses into the pill, and the tab bar still minimises and expands.

comments.body:
**Adversarial review (fable-5.2, mac/M1-r1046-fable, b7cd3901)** — REQUEST CHANGES

1. **High — `App/SwiftHFR/Navigation/TopicListView.swift:45`.** CI is red: the SwiftLint job (0.65.1, `--strict`) fails on `let _ = Self.bodyRuns[...] += 1` (`redundant_discardable_let`). `_ = …` is not legal in a `ViewBuilder`, so either add `redundant_discardable_let: ignore_swiftui_view_bodies: true` to `.swiftlint.yml` (the option exists in 0.65.1) or move the increment into a helper the existing `let loader = …` declaration calls. A PR with a failing required check is not merge-ready.

2. **Medium — `App/SwiftHFRTests/Navigation/FavorisScrollHostedTests.swift:91`, class coverage.** The guard only counts `TopicListView.body`. Mutation: `let _ = titleVisibility.isHeaderVisible` inside `header(_:title:)`'s `HStack` (a per-frame read in a section header: every header rebuilds per crossing, O(sections), suspect 2 of #1015) → the test **passes**. The seam catches the one pre-#1017 dependency, not the class the issue describes. Fix: count header and row builds too (`bodyRuns` keyed by model + a `headerBuilds`/`rowBuilds` counter at `header(_:title:)` and `rows(_:)`), and assert all three stay flat; the PR body's probe already measured them, ship those counters.

3. **Medium — same file:68-72 and `:86-89`, LESSONS 3.** The suite doc and the PR body say the test covers "the bars moving" / "the tab bar minimises". It does not: a programmatic scroll never triggers the Liquid Glass minimise (the body admits it), and the stand-in (`additionalSafeAreaInsets` steps on the hosting controller) is not shown to be what the minimise does. Say so in the test comment and in the PR body's "Tests" (covered: large-title crossings; not covered: the real minimise), or drive the minimise for real.

4. **Low — `:84`, positive control.** The crossing is inferred from `indexPathsForVisibleItems` (item 0,0), never from the SwiftUI side that triggers the class (`onScrollVisibilityChange` → `TitleVisibility`). If a SwiftUI change stops that callback on programmatic offsets, the test passes trivially (LESSONS 2). Count `PillSlot` renders (or expose `TitleVisibility` in the seam) and assert ≥ 2 flips.

5. **Low — `:56-58`.** The comment says "as `FavoritesTabView` builds it", but the host omits `FavoritesSourceMenu` toolbar item, `preferredCompactColumn`, `TabSplitWidth`, `filteredPosts`, `ExperimentalSettings`/density environment. Host `FavoritesTabView` with a fake `ReaderServices` (one exists in `ReaderOverflowTests`) or name the omissions.

6. **Detail — `TopicListView.swift:40`.** `#if DEBUG` static counter is acceptable (MainActor-inferred from `View`, no release cost); `ObjectIdentifier` keys are never removed and can be reused after dealloc; the test's baseline-delta copes, say so in the doc comment.

**Verified:** worktree at b7cd3901, `build-for-testing` (iOS 27.2 sim) green; `FavorisScrollHostedTests/scrollLeavesTheListAlone()` passed 3/3 (5.9–7.0 s). Mutation A (body reads `titleVisibility.isHeaderVisible`) → fails at `:91` as the PR claims. Mutation B (header reads it) → passes (finding 2). `gh pr checks 1046`: SwiftLint fail, annotation at `TopicListView.swift:45`. Line lengths ≤ 140 by awk. Claim matches the issue's `/claim mac/M1`; `Refs #1015` is right (no fix, device check pending). Whole target not rerun. Worktree and DerivedData removed.

**Adversarial review (fable-5.2, mac/M1-r1046-fable, delta 1fc0500b)** — APPROVE

Round-1 findings against the delta:
1. SwiftLint (High) — fixed: no `let _ =` in a builder; `counting(_:_:title:)` sits in existing expressions. CI SwiftLint green on 1fc0500b; the only red check is the draft gate ("macOS jobs run when the PR is marked ready", #477), expected.
2. Class coverage (Medium) — fixed: headers (by group id) and rows (by topic id) are counted. My mutation B (per-frame read in `header(_:title:)`'s `HStack`) now fails at `:134`, `:135`, `:150`; mutation C (read in `rows(_:)`'s closure) fails at `:135`.
3. "Bars moving" claim (Medium) — fixed: suite doc (`:9-13`) and PR body say what is covered and that the real tab-bar minimise is not.
4. Positive control (Low) — fixed: `TitleVisibility.reports` ≥ 1 down, ≥ 2 round trip, plus `isHeaderVisible` flips, asserted at `:132` and `:149`.
5. Host fidelity (Low) — fixed: `FavoritesTabView` with a fake `ReaderServices`; omissions named.
6. Key reuse (Detail) — documented on `renders` (`TopicListView+RenderSeam.swift:14-15`).

Checked on the new code:
- `TitleVisibility.report(_:)` (`ScreenTitle.swift:98-104`): production path is `isHeaderVisible = visible`, byte-for-byte the old assignment; `reports` is `@ObservationIgnored` and `#if DEBUG`, so no new dependency for `PillSlot`.
- `TopicListView+RenderSeam.swift`: statics are `#if DEBUG`, MainActor-isolated through `View`'s inference (compiles under strict concurrency); release keeps a generic pass-through and an unused `RenderPart` enum, no state.
- Doc comments present on `RenderPart`, `renders`, `titleVisibilities`, `counting`, `report`; lines ≤ 140 (awk); body matches the code (what is counted, the baseline-delta, mutation list, covered/not covered).

Details, no change required:
- `titleVisibilities` retains every `TitleVisibility` for the process's life (debug only, one small object per list ever shown).
- `hostFavoris` (`:75-95`) shows the window before `#require(found)`; a failing `#require` leaves it visible for the next serialized test. Harmless today; a `defer` inside the helper would close it.

**Verified:** worktree at 1fc0500b, `build-for-testing` (iOS 27.2 sim 3C7DA65A, via xb.sh) green; `FavorisScrollHostedTests` passed 2/2 (5.4–5.8 s); mutations B and C built and failed as above; `gh pr checks 1046`: SwiftLint pass, app job = draft gate; body read at this head. Whole target not rerun. Worktree and DerivedData removed.
